headline: Arena, the website where people vote on which AI chatbot answers better, has raised $200 million at a value of $3.1 billion.
score_reason: Kept at pool score 6: a sizeable round for a widely used ranking service, with figures supplied by the company.
importance_line: What changed is that the rankings many people use to pick an AI model are run by a well-funded company that also sells evaluations to AI labs and businesses, which matters to users choosing models, then to the labs being ranked, and the doubt is that the revenue and visitor figures are Arena's own and the new alignment table is preliminary.
summary: TechCrunch reports that Arena, which began in 2023 as a UC Berkeley research project, said its Series B round (a mid-stage investment round) was led by Lightspeed Venture Partners and Khosla Ventures and nearly doubles the $1.7 billion value it had in January, as its annualized revenue grew from $30 million to $100 million by June, by its own account. It also added an alignment ranking that scores models on behaviour such as taking actions they were not asked to take or "deceptive completion", where OpenAI models currently top the preliminary table.
